clips.title: Stress doesn't kill. Never completing the stress cycle kills.
clips.why: Rewrites the thing half the workforce feels daily. Humans are built for stress rising AND falling; modern life is one unbroken rise from alarm-scroll to last email. The line 'stress doesn't kill — never completing the stress cycle kills' is the kind of sentence that gets screenshotted and argued with, and the adrenal burnout ending gives it a consequence.

clips.title: Nine weeks, 450 students, a digital detox — and the scores moved

video_read: A ~3-hour English-language Raj Shamani podcast with a UC Berkeley cognitive neuroscientist about attention, phones, habits, boredom, burnout and sleep. The best material is a long, even run of counter-intuitive, testable claims about everyday behaviour — a visible phone lowers measured IQ, scrolling doesn't count as a break, boredom is where ideas come from, stress cycles never closing is what kills — with the most striking science clustered in the middle two hours and the most personal material (her own addiction) at the very end.
